messages.subject: workflowr 1.6.1 and useR! 2020
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I apologize I haven't been announcing the latest workflowr releases to this list recently. I skipped the releases of 1.5.0 and 1.6.0. This week I released 1.6.1. If you haven't updated in a while, I highly recommended you do to take advantage of the latest enhancements and bug fixes.

https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/releases/tag/v1.6.1

Also, Peter Carbonetto and I will be giving the tutorial "Create and share reproducible code with R Markdown and workflowr" at useR! in St. Louis this July. Please spread the word!

https://user2020.r-project.org/program/tutorials/

Thanks,

John

Release notes for workflowr 1.6.1:

This patch release of workflowr includes minor improvements, updated documentation, bug fixes, and lots of internal refactoring.
Minor improvements

Workflowr functions check if the working directory exists (idea from @pcarbo <https://github.com/pcarbo>, #185 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/185>)

wflow_use_github() can now create repositories for GitHub organizations using the new argument organization. However, GitLab Groups should still be specified with the argument username for wflow_use_gitlab() (bug report from @stephens999 <https://github.com/stephens999>, #186 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/186>)

Any workflowr function that prompts for user input will continue to re-prompt until valid input has been entered (or canceled by hitting the key Esc) (idea from @pcarbo <https://github.com/pcarbo>)

All functions that commit to the Git repository first check for the availability of the Git variables user.name <http://user.name> and user.email (either global or local), which are required for creating a commit (#85 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/85>)

The workflowr icon is displayed in browser tabs of workflowr websites (idea from @pcarbo <https://github.com/pcarbo>)
Updated documentation

Document that GitLab.com provides private repositories with access control to the source code repository and the website (#187 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/187>)

Update URL to RStudio-specific instructions for installing pandoc (bug report from @PietrH <https://github.com/PietrH>, #190 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/190>)

Document in the FAQ vignette how to include an external image using an absolute URL to the image hosted on another website (idea from @JiaxiangBU <https://github.com/JiaxiangBU>, #159 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/159>)

Document how to embed Shiny apps with knitr::include_app() and shinyapps.io <http://www.shinyapps.io/> (idea from @rsimon64 <https://github.com/rsimon64>, #130 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/130>)

Update the FAQ on including external images to account for the breaking change in knitr::include_graphics() introduced in knitr version 1.28 (bug report from @ditordccaa <https://github.com/ditordccaa>, #103 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/103>)

Add FAQ entry on how to use a Git hosting site that uses the HTTP protocol (idea from @antass <https://github.com/antass>, #163 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/163>)
Bug fixes
Fix Windows-specific bug that caused the table of past versions to be missing from the workflowr report (bug introduced in version 1.5.0)
Internal refactoring

Internal refactoring for increased speed and improved error handling of input arguments

Check for class with inherits() (#189 <https://github.com/jdblischak/workflowr/issues/189>)

Switch to use pandoc option --include-in-header to insert workflowr-specific CSS and other metadata (surprisingly --include-before-body works fine)
